summary: Sub-phase 16.2c is landed in one green sub-step and it REFUTES the plan's exists_tailStable_repr rather than proving it: Fixture.not_tailStable shows no member of the re-presentation family Fixture.certRep a b c is tail-stable, for any pre-period or period multiplier, while Fixture.certRep_slice_shift shows every member presents Fixture.cert's own slice sequence shifted. TailStable is therefore a demand on the frame together with its closure and not on the presentation; the false harmlessness claim on TailStable's docstring is corrected in place and the lemma is absent because it is untrue, not pending. Phase 16 closes as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with that one reasoned exclusion, and Phase 17 is marked [BLOCKED] on the design ruling the refutation forces (four candidate repairs enumerated at its heading). Nothing is stubbed: sorry_count 0, 64/64 new declarations within the three standard axioms, full lake build 2798 jobs with zero errors and zero warnings.

artifacts.summary: Round-4 summary extended with dispatch 38: the re-presentation family, the refutation of exists_tailStable_repr, the two asymmetric failure modes, and the Phase 17 design blocker.
Resume point: Phase 17's blocker is the next action; the one thing a successor must not mis-read, two named open questions, and 9 carried-forward environment hazards including four new ones.

blockers.verbatim_goal: Include `G.BiSerial` and `G.TailStable` as the first two conjuncts of `Certifies`. Both are window-decided and both are already `Decidable`.
blockers.what_was_tried: Sub-phase 16.2c's own route was run to completion and produced a refutation rather than the lemma it was asked for. The re-presentation family Fixture.certRep a b c was built (pre-period absorbed into mid, either period multiplied), certRep_slice_shift proves each member presents Fixture.cert's own slice sequence shifted right by b, and Fixture.not_tailStable proves no member is tail-stable. The mechanism was then traced to its source: Phi_fwd is a reachability transfer; Position.lean's StepClause constrains untl g e in X in terms of the LATER label only; LabCoherent is bottom-freeness plus the implication clause and constrains no eventuality at all.
blockers.why_it_failed: Phase 17's first task bullet rests on a premise sub-phase 16.2c disproved: that TailStable constrains only the presentations a checker accepts, because any unstable certificate could be re-presented (exists_tailStable_repr). Fixture.cert's frame has NO tail-stable presentation. The repair is a change to TailStable's own definition, which is named in this plan's Lean Challenge Statement, is consumed by Phases 18-21, and is the hypothesis hstab of Phase 19's relative-completeness theorem whose landed linchpin tailStable_iff_window is stated from it. That is a design decision, not an implementation detail, so it is escalated rather than guessed. Four candidate repairs, with what each is believed to buy and what is NOT proved about any of them, are enumerated at the plan's Phase 17 heading.

decisions_made: exists_tailStable_repr is NOT stated in any form, because it is false. A weakened version (backward conjunct only, or under an extra closure hypothesis) was considered and rejected: the plan's own Phase 16 Scope Hypothesis forbids weakening a theorem to make it come out true, and a weakened lemma under that name would be read downstream as the harmlessness claim it is not.

The refutation is a FAMILY statement, not a single-certificate one. Proving only not cert.TailStable would have been consistent with the plan, which says an unstable certificate should be re-presented rather than rejected. Hence certRep a b c and not_tailStable (a b c).

The verdict went into a NEW module PlusSlicedCertificate/FixtureStable.lean rather than into Stable.lean, because Stable.lean imports Fixture.lean and the verdict needs both the fixture and Phi_fwd. Merging the two modules was the alternative and was rejected on the grounds the 16.1 record already gave for separating them.

The two failure modes are two separately named theorems, not one. Phi_back_L0_ne_cert is the pre-period showing through and IS repaired by the recipe (not_mem_L0_pR); Phi_fwd_R0_ne is repaired by nothing. Collapsing them would have hidden the asymmetry that makes this a design problem rather than a fixture artifact.

not_mem_L0_pR is stated only about the witness, not about Phi_back L0 = L0. It says the backward failure's witness leaves L0 once 1 <= b; it does NOT claim certRep a b c satisfies the backward conjunct, and its docstring says so.

Phase 17 is marked [BLOCKED] rather than started with a guessed repair, and Phase 16 is closed as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] rather than [PARTIAL], because nothing in Phase 16 changes whichever way the ruling goes and there is no residual Phase 16 work to hand off.
